title: Canonical derived augmentation on an injective resolution
statement: For an abelian category $\mathcal A$ with its ordinary derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], define $Q_{\mathbb N}:C^{\geq0}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ by extension by zero to integer degrees followed by $Q$. Now let $R,S$ be ring sheaves on small sites with their module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their derived categories, and K-injective resolutions on $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Let $G:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ be additive, with the ordinary right-derived functor and its canonical unit $\eta_G$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For an injective resolution $i:K[0]\to I$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], define $c_{G,I}:RG(Q_{\mathbb N}K[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathbb N}(GI)$ as the composite of $RG(Qi)$, the inverse of $\eta_G$ at the extended injective complex $I$, and the canonical isomorphism commuting $G$ with extension by zero. For a coherent Cech image model $D$ [def-sfb-coherent-cech-image-model], a sheaf $V$ and a chain map $b:GI\to T_D(G,V,I)$ to its nonnegative signed total [def-sp-double-complex-total], define $\alpha_{D,G,V,I,b}=c_{G,I}\,;\,Q_{\mathbb N}(b):RG(Q_{\mathbb N}K[0])\to Q(T_D(G,V,I))$. The definition applies to every such $b$; when $b$ is the localization-unit augmentation of $D$, it is the canonical derived Cech augmentation. It asserts no invertibility or naturality theorem.
